prompt:
The graph shows the variation with thermodynamic temperature T of the root-mean-square speed c_rms of the molecules of an ideal gas.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Graph of root-mean-square speed c_rms on the vertical axis against thermodynamic temperature T on the horizontal axis, starting at the origin (0,0) and curving upward with a positive, decreasing gradient (square-root curve).]
(a) State the relationship between c_rms and thermodynamic temperature T. [1]
(b) Explain why the graph passes through the origin (0,0) and why its gradient decreases as T increases. [2]
(c) On the same axes, sketch the curve that would be obtained for a gas with a larger molecular mass, and give a reason for your sketch. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) States that c_rms is directly proportional to the square root of thermodynamic temperature T (or c_rms proportional to sqrt(T)).
(b) Origin: At absolute zero (T = 0 K), translational kinetic energy is zero, so molecular speed is zero.
(b) Decreasing gradient: Since c_rms proportional to T^(1/2), the gradient dc_rms/dT is proportional to T^(-1/2) = 1 / (2 sqrt(T)), which decreases as T increases.
(c) Curve lies below the original curve at all temperatures because c_rms is proportional to 1 / sqrt(m), so for a larger molecular mass m, c_rms is smaller at any given temperature.

hints: In (a), state the square-root relationship from c_rms = sqrt(3kT / m).
In (b), consider what happens at T = 0 K and the mathematical derivative of a square root function.
In (c), how does molecular mass affect speed at the same temperature?
solution:
(a) The root-mean-square speed is directly proportional to the square root of the thermodynamic temperature: c_rms proportional to sqrt(T).
(b) Origin: At absolute zero (T = 0 K), all classical translational molecular motion ceases (E_K = 0), so c_rms = 0, meaning the curve passes through (0,0).
Decreasing gradient: Because c_rms is proportional to T^(1/2), its rate of change with temperature dc_rms/dT is proportional to 1 / sqrt(T). As T increases, 1 / sqrt(T) decreases, so the gradient of the curve decreases.
(c) The curve for a gas of larger molecular mass lies below the original curve at all temperatures. Reason: c_rms = sqrt(3kT / m) is inversely proportional to sqrt(m). At any given temperature, heavier molecules have lower speeds on average.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Look for c_rms proportional to sqrt(T).
Part (b): Award 1 mark for origin (T = 0 K => E_K = 0 => c_rms = 0) and 1 mark for calculus/derivative argument showing gradient decreases as 1/sqrt(T).
Part (c): Award 1 mark for stating/sketching the curve below the original and justifying via c_rms proportional to 1/sqrt(m).
